title: The Score Averager
description: Use array_filter(), array_sum(), and count() to calculate the average of the remaining scores after removing any scores below 50. Output the final average as a raw number.

title: Associative Merge
description: Write code to merge two associative arrays so values from the second array ($newSettings) overwrite the first ($defaultSettings) when the keys overlap. Then, print the final array as a JSON string using json_encode().

title: Order Summary
description:
Filter the array of orders, keeping only those with a status of 'paid'. Sum their totals, select their customer names (preserving input order), and print the summary in the exact format:
Paid customers: Alice, Carla, Dan
Total paid: 245.75
expected_output:
Paid customers: Alice, Carla, Dan
Total paid: 245.75

title: The User Data Sanitizer
description:
Clean, filter, and transform the user data array. Perform the following steps:
1. Filter: Remove any users who are marked as inactive.
2. Sanitize: Trim whitespace from names and ensure all emails are lowercase.
3. Transform: Format names to Title Case (e.g. '  alice smith ' becomes 'Alice Smith').
4. Output the result array using json_encode().

title: The Inventory Auditor
description: Write code that processes an inventory array. Filter out any products that have a stock_count of 0. Calculate the total value of the remaining inventory (Price x Stock). Output a single string: 'In stock: [Product Names separated by commas]. Total Value: $[Total]'.
expected_output: In stock: Keyboard, Monitor, Laptop, Charger, Headset. Total Value: $4060

title: The Coupon Validator
description: Iterate through a list of order totals. Apply a 15% discount only to orders that are $100 or more. Format all the resulting prices to 2 decimal places (so they are strings), and output the outer processed array as a JSON string using json_encode().
focus: Loop logic, conditional updates, and number formatting

title: The Category Totals
description: Group the grocery items by category and compute the total cost of all items in that category rounded to 2 decimal places. Sort the resulting associative array alphabetically by category name (key) using ksort(), and output the result as a JSON string via json_encode().

title: Reverse String Practice
description: Reverse the given string using strrev().
